summary: Theorem A.3 includes the entire semi-infinite spectrum at a prescribed exponential pseudospectral scale; unilateral shift disproves this term. No damage to the inspected A.4 ->6.1 ->6.2 path established.

problems.claim: Lambda(A)+Delta_epsilon subset Lambda_epsilon(A_N,l) for epsilon=C rho^N, any r<1,rho>r, constant independent of N.
problems.assumptions: Bounded semi-infinite Toeplitz backward shift a1=1,ak=0 otherwise,l=1,f(z)=z;r=1/4,rho=1/2,lambda=3/4. All printed bandwidth and radius hypotheses hold.
problems.decisive_evidence: lambda is an l2 eigenvalue of the infinite operator; ||(lambda I-J_N)^-1|| <=4((4/3)^N-1), so C 2^-N times the resolvent tends to zero. Eventually lambda is outside the finite epsilon-pseudospectrum for every fixed finite C.
problems.counterevidence: Natural residual lambda^N remains exponentially small. The example rejects prescribed faster scale for entire spectrum, not all localization. Cited 1992 primary theorem has same notation.
problems.core_dependency: A.4 omits the bad term and has a separate construction; 6.1 explicitly uses A.4, 6.2 uses Proposition5.9. No dependency of main rigorous localization argument on this term found.
problems.impact: Local recalled theorem is false; no refutation of the physical gauge-matrix family or main residual estimates established.
problems.correction: For this term, replace Lambda(A) by Lambda(A_N,l). Eigenvector residual directly proves corrected finite-spectrum disk inclusion. Remaining terms/uniformity require their own proof.

unconfirmed_observations.reason: Residual theorems do not alone control eigenvector distances, but no counterexample within the physical family was established; paper also uses numerical evidence and acknowledges open exact-decay question.

independent_acceptance_review.coverage_scope_check: The report limits the confirmed defect to the spectrum-thickening term of A.3. It identifies static code reading, unproved numerical behavior and incomplete A.4 uniformity checks separately. This acceptance does not execute author code or infer exact eigenvector failure from a pseudospectral example.

problems.source_claim: A.3 on PDF page 33 includes Lambda(A)+Delta_epsilon for epsilon=C*rho^N, C independent of N, for every r<1,rho>r. A is the semi-infinite operator defined on pages 31-32.
problems.hypotheses: The backward shift with a_1=1 and all other coefficients zero is a bounded banded Toeplitz operator; l=1, r=1/4, rho=1/2, lambda=3/4 meet all printed hypotheses. The full-spectrum term needs no membership in Omega_r.
problems.independent_argument: The l2 vector (lambda^j)_(j>=0) proves lambda is in Lambda(A). Finite J_N is nilpotent. The exact finite geometric resolvent sum has norm at most sum_(k=0)^(N-1) lambda^(-k-1)=4*((4/3)^N-1). Multiplication by C*2^(-N) tends to zero, so for every finite C, sufficiently large N puts lambda outside the claimed epsilon-pseudospectrum. This proves the uniform-rate contradiction without a numerical approximation.
problems.counterevidence: The example has geometric residual at the slower lambda^N rate. It does not exclude geometric localization generally. Replacing only the bad term by the finite spectrum plus its epsilon disk is justified by the eigenvector residual identity; no proof of the remaining uniformity claims is inferred.
problems.impact_and_severity: Source page 19 explicitly invokes A.4, whose separate root/boundary construction omits the disproved term; the transferred tail estimate is a residual argument. Minor reflects the absence of this term from the inspected core proof path, not appendix position or ease of repair.
problems.repair: The finite-spectrum disk replacement is proved for that term only. Main physical-family exact eigenvectors and original experiments are not refuted.
